A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPHERE and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. Their shared benchmark and retained results support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original VLM evaluations on SPHERE, including task accuracy, viewpoint comparisons, intermediate-information experiments, and appendix validity scores.

after.justification: v4 retains these original evaluations and adds results for further models and qualitative examples of model responses.

M1.justification: SPHERE's hierarchical task design and intermediate/final-question decomposition remain unchanged. The expanded reasoning explanation introduces no new proposed method component; the prompt amendment concerns evaluation settings.

E1.justification: Both versions describe the same 2,285-question COCO-2017 benchmark, with four single-skill, three multi-skill, and two reasoning tasks and identical sample counts in Table 2. The new appendix examples illustrate retained coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds Qwen2.5-VL (7B and 72B) and Janus-Pro (7B) to the accuracy, viewpoint, intermediate-information, and validity comparisons in Tables 3–5 and 7. All previously evaluated models remain, making this a limited comparator expansion.

E3.justification: The explicitly specified intermediate-information prompt in Section 4.3 gains 'Answer the question directly.' This is a limited reported testing-procedure revision, although the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun. Dataset counts and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 4–5 extend the existing viewpoint and intermediate-information analyses to the added models. Appendix B adds GPT-4o and Gemini success/failure examples across all nine tasks, illustrating viewpoint, counting, size, and reasoning difficulties. This expands qualitative diagnosis without a new systematic robustness study.

E5.justification: Both versions average five differently seeded evaluations and retain the same dataset goodness-of-fit tests in Appendix A and Table 6. v4 introduces no new uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or statistical comparison procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 3–5 and 7 add results for three model configurations while retaining all earlier numerical rows. Qwen2.5-VL (72B) achieves 64.3% overall, taking second place from Gemini 2.0 Flash at 61.7%; GPT-4o remains first at 67.9%. Tables 8–10 also add qualitative response outcomes.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The new discussion of Piaget and object permanence is conceptual motivation, not a formal theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical evaluation, the human-annotated benchmark, and VLM spatial weaknesses. The changed availability statement concerns access rather than the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds an interpretation that spatial-model techniques benefit spatial capabilities, while suggesting task-specific training and generalization gaps explain remaining weaknesses. Section 3.2.1 adds cognitive-development and object-permanence motivation. The explicit limitations in Section 6 are unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 replaces the promised future release with a benchmark repository link. Section 4.1 newly documents default model-demo prompt templates and hyperparameters, gives the direct-answer instruction, and changes the hardware description from one RTX 3090 GPU to GPUs.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to the Qwen2.5-VL technical report and Janus-Pro paper for the new evaluated models. The related-work discussion and positioning of SPHERE against earlier spatial benchmarks remain substantively stable.

P1.justification: v4 renames Sections 3 and 3.1 to 'The SPHERE Benchmark' and 'Overview', corrects wording and author spelling, and adds localized explanatory and acknowledgement text. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds a substantial illustrated appendix in Tables 8–10, pairing images and questions with ground truth and GPT-4o/Gemini answers across all nine tasks. Some earlier examples are reused, but the systematic visual presentation is new. Existing result tables gain rows and revised rank highlighting; Figures 1–10 are retained with minor resizing or reflow.

improvement.justification: The repository link and clearer prompt/default-setting documentation address limited usability and reproducibility gaps in v2. Additional model comparisons and illustrated success/failure cases make the benchmark easier to assess. These are useful incremental gains; the benchmark design and central findings remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish rerunning retained results under the amended prompt.
